canonical_name: hashicorp/memberlist 0.5.4 -- SWIM-style gossip membership and failure detection (the machinery under Consul, Nomad, Serf)
lineage: Das, Gupta, Motivala's SWIM (2002): scalable weakly-consistent membership by randomized probing (ping, ping-req through k peers, suspect, dead) with gossip dissemination -- the asynchronous, timeout-based failure detector that Serf (2013), Consul and Nomad run on. Lifeguard extensions (2018). Distinct assumptions from Raft: no leader, no log, eventual membership agreement, suspicion timeouts instead of quorum.
compiler_or_interpreter: go 1.22 (docker golang:1.22-bookworm; modules fetched at run time, recorded)
dependencies: Go modules (go.sum pinned in the tree)
entry_points: memberlist.Create(config); Join; the probe loop (state.go: probeNode, suspect, dead); go test -run 'TestMemberlist_(Probe|Suspect|Gossip)'

example.input: in-process members over loopback with deliberately unreachable peers
example.output: the suspect -> dead transitions the tests assert (the ORACLE)

upstream_docs: Das, Gupta, Motivala, SWIM: Scalable Weakly-consistent Infection-style Process Group Membership Protocol, DSN 2002
Dadgar, Phanishayee, Lifeguard: Local Health Awareness for More Accurate Failure Detection, 2018

human_capability_summary.built_to: let every node in a cluster learn who is alive and who has died, without a coordinator, tolerating message loss and slow nodes
human_capability_summary.pressure: asynchronous network: lost probes, slow peers, partitions; false positives cost as much as misses
human_capability_summary.success_means: a dead node is declared dead within the suspicion timeout; a slow-but-alive node is refuted via indirect probes

human_failure_condition: a partition splits membership; a live node is wrongly declared dead and evicted
behavioral_entry_point: the tests' unreachable peers and timeouts; shrink ProbeTimeout / SuspicionMult and watch false positives

lineage_relations.note: two answers to 'who is alive': gossip suspicion vs leader heartbeats

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run hashicorp-memberlist-0.5.4
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: let every node in a cluster learn who is alive and who has died, without a coordinator, tolerating message loss and slow nodes
